Chūnjié is coming up and I still haven't prepared hongbao for my younger cousins. How would you handle that?

Chūnjié (Chinese New Year) is a significant holiday, and giving hongbao (red envelopes with money) to younger relatives is a traditional and meaningful custom. If you're running short on time, here are a few suggestions to help you prepare: 1. **Buy red envelopes in bulk**: You can find red envelopes at most Asian markets or online. Buying in bulk will save you time and ensure you have enough for all your younger cousins. 2. **Prepare the money**: Decide on the amount you want to give to each cousin and prepare the cash in advance. You can also consider giving smaller amounts to younger cousins and larger amounts to older ones. 3. **Add a personal touch**: Consider adding a small note or a Chinese New Year's greeting card to each envelope to make it more special and personalized. 4. **Ask for help**: If you're really short on time, ask a family member or a friend to help you prepare the hongbao. This can be a fun and collaborative activity. 5. **Digital hongbao**: If you're unable to prepare physical hongbao, consider sending digital red envelopes through mobile payment apps like WeChat or Alipay. This is a convenient and modern way to give hongbao, especially if you're unable to meet your cousins in person. Remember, the most important aspect of giving hongbao is the thought and love behind it. Your cousins will appreciate the gesture, regardless of how last-minute it may be. Gong Xi Fa Cai! (Wishing you prosperity and good fortune!)
